title: Judges
author: The author is not named; Jewish tradition has often connected the book with Samuel.
date: After Joshua and before the monarchy, covering Israel's early life in the land.
audience: Israel, showing the danger of turning from the Lord and the need for righteous deliverance.
historicalSetting: Judges describes repeated cycles of sin, oppression, crying out, and deliverance during a time when Israel lacked faithful leadership.
themes: The danger of everyone doing what is right in his own eyes
keyVerse: Judges 21:25 — "In those days there was no king in Israel. Everyone did that which was right in his own eyes."
christFocus: Judges exposes the need for a perfect Deliverer and righteous King. The failures of Israel and the temporary judges point forward to Jesus Christ, the true Savior and King.
outline: Cycles of oppression and deliverance — Judges 3-16
